name: Ampicillin
executiveSummary: Aminopenicillin. Usual adult IV/PO 0.5–2 g every 4–6 h (meningitis up to ~12 g/day); pediatrics 100–200 mg/kg/day (meningitis 300–400 mg/kg/day). Cornerstone in neonatal sepsis/meningitis per NNU protocol.
indications:
## Indications

- ENT, respiratory, genitourinary, GI, skin/soft-tissue, endocarditis, meningitis, and bacteremia due to susceptible organisms (streptococci, enterococci, *Listeria*, some non–beta-lactamase–producing gram-negatives).
- Empiric neonatal sepsis (usually with an aminoglycoside).

## Precautions

- Penicillin allergy. High rash risk with mononucleosis / allopurinol.
- Prefer dilution in **NS** (dextrose accelerates hydrolysis).
- Adjust interval in renal failure.

> Confirm susceptibility; does not cover ESBL or MRSA.

adulto.presentation: Vial 500 mg–1 g; PO capsules 250–500 mg (if available).
adulto.dose: PO: **250–500 mg every 6 h**. IV/IM: mild–moderate **0.5–1 g every 6 h**; severe **1–2 g every 4–6 h**. Meningitis / severe endovascular: up to **2 g every 4 h** (usual max **12 g/day**).
adulto.administration: IV push: reconstitute 1 g in 10–15 mL sterile water; give over ≥ 10–15 min (max ~100 mg/min). Intermittent IV: dilute in 50–100 mL NS (~10 mg/mL) over 15–60 min. Prefer NS over 5% dextrose.
adulto.notes: Concentrated reconstituted (~100 mg/mL): short stability (hours refrigerated); prepare close to administration.

pediatrico.presentation: Vial 500–1000 mg; PO suspension by brand.
pediatrico.dose: **100 mg/kg/day every 6 h** (mild–moderate). Pneumonia / severe: **200 mg/kg/day every 6 h**. Meningitis: **300–400 mg/kg/day every 6 h** (max **12 g/day**).
pediatrico.administration: IV: reconstitute with sterile water; dilute 2–30 mg/mL; push 3–5 min or infusion 15–30 min. PO if tolerated and focus appropriate.
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight. See renal adjustment table.

neonatal.dose: Orientative term neonate: **50 mg/kg/dose every 12 h** (non-meningitic). Meningitis / *Listeria*: more frequent dosing per center gestational/postnatal age table.
neonatal.notes: Always cross-check the institutional neonatal card (PMA/PNA).

stability:
## Stability

- Concentrated reconstituted: ~1 h room temp / ~4 h refrigerated (check label).
- Diluted in NS: ~4 h room temp / ~24 h refrigerated (pediatric cards often 8 h / 48 h).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, glossitis, rash/urticaria, eosinophilia, anemia, thrombocytopenia. Anaphylaxis in allergic patients.
